evidence:
Measured on grok 0.2.112 (2026-07-26, t-4e6ba5) by asking a live agent under `--permission-mode default` to delete a file OUTSIDE its workspace, then capturing the pane. Verbatim tail:
    ┃  Remove target.txt from /tmp/grok-outside
    ┃  rm -f /tmp/grok-outside/target.txt
    ┃
    ┃  1 (●) Yes, and don't ask again for anything (always-approve mode)
    ┃  2 (○) Yes, proceed
    ┃  3 (○) No, reject (type to add feedback)
    ┃
    1/3:select  │  Ctrl+o:always-approve  │  Ctrl+c:cancel
Nothing in the base manifest matches this chrome: there is no [y/n], no 'do you want to', and the numbered options are '1 (●)' with NO period, so base's '❯\s*\d+\.' menu rule misses them. The pane also keeps changing while the prompt waits (an elapsed-time counter ticks every second), which is why the agent stayed 'working' and governed input was refused as busy. The footer is the bottom-most line, so matching it keeps distanceFromBottom at 0 and lets classifyForPrecedence beat that content churn — the first option line sits 4 non-empty lines up, past PATTERN_POSITION_TOLERANCE. NOTE for whoever answers: the highlighted option is SESSION STATE, not a constant. A first prompt highlights option 1 (always-approve); after answering '2' the next prompt arrives with '2 (●)'. A bare Enter therefore sends an unpredictable decision, and on a first prompt that decision is blanket approval. Answer with an explicit digit. Verified on the live pane: sending '2' performed the single action, left the footer WITHOUT 'always-approve', and the next out-of-workspace action prompted again — so the one-time grant really is one-time.

rules.evidence: Two independent signatures of the same modal, both measured above. The footer is matched because it is the bottom-most line; the radio options are matched so a variant that drops or reworks the footer still registers.
